text:
oncall-bot: ALERT: apiserver liveness probe failing in eu-central-2 (instance set eu-cp-2). 4/5 restarts in last 8m. auto-escalation to eng-sre.

mika: seeing controller-manager leader flip noise + GPU node onboarding stuck. lots of pods in ContainerCreating.

jordan: any apiserver logs? status codes?

sam: pasted tail of kube-apiserver log snippet: 
```
I0318 12:04:11.123456 1 healthcheck.go:45] liveness probe failed: context deadline exceeded
E0318 12:04:11.456789 1 handler.go:212] GET /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods: etcdserver: request timed out\n```

lee: etctd metrics look noisy — WAL fsync p95 jumped, etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds_bucket shows spike about 12:02. linking graph: https://metrics/reports/etcd/eu-central-2 (view restricted).

ana: @ana here — NAT gateway egress in eu-central-2 showed SNAT exhaustion earlier, but that was at 11:50 and cleared. wondering if a brief I/O hiccup on control-plane hosts (noisy neighbor on shared nvme) caused WAL latency. vm host event logs?

mika: ran `kubectl get endpoints -n kube-system kube-apiserver` — one endpoint missing (eu-cp-2-01). rest are fine.

jordan: if the kube-apiserver process is flapping due to failing liveness, controller-manager sees API 500s and restarts leadership election -> GPU provisioning control loops back off. we need to cut traffic off the flapping instance. can we cordon/control-plane traffic?

sam: from control plane fabric: marking node eu-cp-2-01 unhealthy in LB. `lbctl set-weight eu-cp-2-01 0` did reduce errors immediately. errors/5xx dropped by ~70% in the next minute.

lee: good quick mitigation. follow-up: collect iostat/dmesg from host eu-cp-2-01 before we recycle. suspect NVMe stall. requesting ops-owner.

ana: putting a temporary autoscale on etcd followers? careful, we can't just add replicas without snapshot sync. prefer to reprovision the host or migrate disks off host then remount. ops: eu-cp-2-01 on-call?

opsbot: ACTIONS ADDED: [mitigate-lb-eu-cp-2-01], [collect-host-logs-eu-cp-2-01], [inspect-wal-eu-2-12:00-12:10], assignees: mika, sam, lee.

mika: opened host ticket with infra: ticket #INF-6421. asked for nvme SMART and kernel oops around 12:00. also kicked kube-apiserver to restart after logs collected.

jordan: short-term routing fix + restart seems fine. long-term: consider raising apiserver liveness threshold for this zone? or make LB healthcheck absorb transient WAL fsync spikes so controller-manager elections don't cascade.

sam: note — this incident exposed a coupling: GPU onboarding controller retries are exponential and saturate apiserver under leader churn. we should add backpressure in controller or route provisioning to dedicated capacity for heavy onboarding bursts.

lee: agreed. post-incident follow-ups: investigate disk tail latency, add host-level I/O alerts, add apiserver health smoothing (5s->15s for liveness in eu-central-2), and add rate-limit guard on onboarding controller.

mika: current status: eu-cp-2-01 removed from LB, apiserver replicas stable, controller-manager leaders stable, GPU onboarding backlog draining slowly. will keep monitoring for 2 hours.

ana: cost note — if we route heavy onboarding to dedicated capacity, that temporarily increases reserved usage; ops finance FYI.

opsbot: INCIDENT NOTE: incident mitigated by LB weight 0 on eu-cp-2-01 and kube-apiserver restart. follow-up checklist created: INF-6421, SRE-6153 (apiserver-liveness-tune), SRE-6154 (onboarding-rate-limit).

mika: thanks everyone. I'll draft a short postmortem if SMART logs confirm nvme stalls. tagging eng-ml and product to flag possible customer onboarding delays. :thumbsup:
